attributes.fears: that abundance would make her worthless
attributes.how_she_counts: Thirty-one, and the number is exact because it is narrow: she counts the crossings where the water was her responsibility, from RR 172 on, which is about one a year - the same rate Ysoly has kept for thirty. She has actually been out on the plain forty-six times. The other fifteen she made as a hand, and she will tell you flatly that they were somebody else's water and do not belong on her count. This crossing is the thirty-second, and she will not count it until the wagons are off the salt.
attributes.origin: Bell Harrow; came out on the salt at fourteen
attributes.tell: says the ration figure aloud each dawn before anyone asks
attributes.the_brackening: She was there. Twenty-four years old, ten years on the salt, barrel-hand on the second of the two southbound crossings that drank at Sixty Wells in RR 166. She filled from the shafts the taster's board had chalked sweet that morning; the board was a day behind the water, and that is the whole of what went wrong. By the time the teams began refusing the trough her crossing was six days out and past turning back, so it went south on what it had, and the seven days to the Dry Ferry are the days she does not describe. The dying did not stop at the Ferry. She came off at the far rim with something under half the people she had gone in with, and came home to Bell Harrow the next season on somebody else's water. The two hundred are not on her count and she does not claim them - she was not the one measuring. Everything she does now she learned in that field: the weighing, the counting aloud, the ration figure said at dawn before anybody can ask for it, because a number somebody chalked yesterday killed people she knew.
attributes.voice: dry, numerical, superstitious about waste; speaks in weights and days and will correct you on both
attributes.wants: to finish her last crossings the way she began them
attributes.water_master_since: RR 172, at thirty. Sixteen years a barrel-hand before that, from RR 156.
attributes.why_it_matters_in_chapter_2: Chapter 2 opens the packet at Sixty Wells, which puts the news that there is fresh water under the plain in front of the one person on the train who was standing in this field when it went bad. Two things land on her, and the second is not the one Denet is braced for. The first is her own fear arriving on schedule: if the centre can be dug with a shovel, a woman whose whole expertise is moving fifty-two head across eight hundred miles on what nine wagons will carry has a trade nobody needs. The second takes her longer. If the survey is right, the people who got past the Ferry that year walked over the centre on day twenty with brine in their barrels and fourteen feet of sweet water under their boots. The two hundred did not die of the plain. They died of nobody being able to read the ground. She will not say any of this at the fire. She will say the ration figure, and then go and work the field - sixty stone collars, and she tastes every shaft herself before a barrel goes under it, because she has not taken the taster's board's word for anything in thirty-seven years.

name: Sabra Onn
summary: Water-master of Ysoly's train, sixty-one, and the oldest hand on it; she measures out every ration by weight and has not lost a traveller to thirst in the thirty-one crossings she counts, which are the thirty-one where the water was hers. She was at Sixty Wells in RR 166 - twenty-four, a barrel-hand, filling from a shaft the taster's board still called sweet - and came off the far rim with something under half the people she went in with. Her whole discipline is scarcity, so a sea under the plain does not read to her as deliverance but as the end of the only expertise she has. She counts aloud and considers spilled water something close to a sin.
